chart_specs.purpose: Show that forecasters mostly guessed too low on benchmark progress, but not always, so the reader sees both directions of error in one view.
chart_specs.data_file: data/forecast_vs_actual.csv (does not exist yet; build from FRI 2026-09-22 and AI Digest 2026-01-16)
chart_specs.encoding: One row per question, sorted by size of miss. Hollow dot = forecast (median; for LEAP/XPT use the expert median, with the superforecaster median as a second smaller dot), filled dot = actual, joined by a line. Line colour: accent (burnt orange) for 'AI came in above forecast', ink grey for 'AI came in below forecast', dashed for unresolved. Percent questions on a shared 0-100% axis: FrontierMath T1-3 end-2025 (31%/30% vs 40.7%), LiveCodeBench Pro Hard end-2026 (14%/12% vs 53.8% as of May 2026, unresolved), Cybench 2025 (62% vs 82%), OSWorld 2025 (60% vs 66.3%), SWE-bench Verified 2025 (88% vs 80.9%), bio uplift (virologists 40%, biosecurity experts 22.5%, superforecasters 16.2% vs 5.2%). METR 80% horizon (3.4h/3.5h vs 3.1h as of May 2026, unresolved) as a separate small panel in hours. Optional inset: IMO gold year, forecast 2030 (experts) / 2035 (superforecasters) vs actual July 2025.
chart_specs.interactions: Hover a row to show forecaster group, forecast date, resolution date, source and provenance tag. Toggle between expert and superforecaster medians where both exist. Unresolved rows labelled 'not yet resolved'.
chart_specs.caveat_label: Forecasts are medians from different panels and dates. FRI notes its review is biased toward finding underestimates. FrontierMath score predates Epoch's finding of errors in ~42% of problems. AI Digest pool was self-selected.

chart_specs.purpose: Show both halves of 'cheaper and better' at once: the price-capability frontier moving left (same ECI for less) and up (more ECI for the same price) across three dates.
chart_specs.encoding: x = blended list price $/M tokens (3:1 input:output), log scale; y = ECI. For each snapshot (2025-11-07, 2026-05-07, 2026-11-07) keep models with release_date <= snapshot and draw a step line of max ECI at or below each price. Latest snapshot in the accent colour, earlier two as faded ink lines. Points as dots, hollow for open weights. Horizontal reference line at ECI 150 (GPT-5 level) with the cheapest crossing marked at each snapshot ($3.44, $1.13, $0.20); vertical reference line at $4 with best ECI marked (150.0, ~152, 168.9). Optional vertical whiskers for ECI credible intervals.
chart_specs.interactions: Toggle or slider to step through the three snapshots (earlier frontiers stay as faded ghosts); hover a dot for model, lab, release date, ECI with interval, input/output price and price source; toggle to show/hide unpriced or third-party-priced models.
chart_specs.caveat_label: List price per token at today's prices for all three dates (historical prices pending). Ignores how many tokens a model uses; effort settings can change cost per task about 10x. ECI scores are Epoch's 7 Nov 2026 vintage. Our calculation.

chart_specs.purpose: Optional second view: cost per question at a fixed accuracy, which counts tokens actually used, showing the ~13x/yr decline independently of per-token list prices.
chart_specs.data_file: external: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/droodman/inference-cost/main/output/slides/Figure%202.csv (not yet in research/data; must be downloaded and verified)
chart_specs.encoding: x = date; y = cost per question in US$, log scale; one step line per accuracy level (e.g. GPQA Diamond 75% above chance, FrontierMath 75%), each step labelled with the cheapest model reaching that level. Annotate Epoch's 13x/yr average.
chart_specs.interactions: Hover a step for model, date, cost per question; toggle benchmark.
chart_specs.caveat_label: Verified (Epoch AI, 22 Sep 2026). Cost-record steps only, five benchmarks, no standard errors. Epoch's source misdates o3 to 31 Jan 2025 (actual release 16 Apr 2025); correct before plotting.

chart_specs.purpose: Show the 50% time horizon rising from seconds to about two working days, the 2024 step-up in pace, and the point where the measuring stick stops working, so readers see both the speed and why the public curve can't answer the 2025-26 acceleration question.
chart_specs.encoding: x = release date (2019-02 to 2026-11, leaving visible empty space after April 2026). y = p50 horizon in minutes, log scale, with human-readable tick labels (1 min, 10 min, 1 h, 4 h, 8 h, 16 h, 2 days, 1 week). sota=true points are filled ink dots with vertical lo-hi 95% interval bars. sota=false points (GPT-5.3-Codex, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4, Claude 3 Opus, GPT-4 Turbo, Claude 4/4.1 Opus, GPT-5.1-Codex-Max) are hollow grey dots. Two fitted lines (our OLS on SOTA points with p50 <=16h): pre-2024 fit (doubling ~260 d), dashed grey, drawn over 2019-2023; 2024+ fit (doubling ~105 d), solid accent (burnt orange), drawn 2024-01 to 2026-04, then dotted beyond with no extrapolation past the band. A horizontal shaded band from 960 min (16 h) upward labelled 'METR: measurements above 16 h unreliable'. A vertical rule at 2026-09-08 labelled 'Leaderboard no longer updated'. Optional annotation for GPT-5.6 Sol (Jun 2026, not in the JSON; from METR's 26 Jun 2026 post): an open marker at 11.3 h with a dotted arrow up to '>270 h if cheating counts', labelled 'not a robust measurement'. Toggle: a second series for the p80 horizon (same file, field p80) in a lighter tint, to show the reliability gap.
chart_specs.interactions: Hover a dot for model name (humanised from key), release date, 50% horizon in h/min with 95% interval, and 80% horizon. Toggle 50% / 50%+80%. Toggle the fitted lines on and off. Each tooltip carries a 'Verified: METR' tag; the fitted lines carry an 'Our calculation' tag. Must work at phone width (labels can collapse into a legend).
chart_specs.caveat_label: Verified: METR Time Horizon 1.1 data (file as of 8 May 2026, page frozen 8 Sep 2026). Trend lines: our calculation. Pre-2023 points are stitched from METR's older suite. Above 16 h the suite cannot measure reliably; the top points are effectively lower bounds with very wide intervals. Software tasks only.

chart_specs.purpose: Show at a glance that AI's standing relative to humans varies enormously by domain, and that the most striking 'beyond humans' results often carry weaker evidence labels.
chart_specs.data_file: research/data/jagged_map.csv (not yet created; build from s4 footnotes: one row per domain with columns domain, tier, comparison_text, ai_value, human_value, date, provenance, footnote_id)
chart_specs.encoding: Y: one row per domain (12 rows: robotics, ARC-AGI-3, Remote Labor Index, forecasting, IMO 2026, Waymo, Pakistan RCT diagnosis, GPQA, hurricane tracks, GenCast weather, Erdős research math, ICPC 2025), sorted by tier. X: ordinal five-step axis 'far below humans' / 'below humans' / 'level with the best' / 'ahead of trained or typical people' / 'beyond the best humans'. Dot colour = evidence quality using site provenance tags: Verified (official or peer-reviewed), Vendor-reported, and a hollow/outlined dot for company claims not officially confirmed (IMO 2026). Optional ghost dot for ARC-AGI-3 at launch (<1%, March 2026) connected by an arrow to Astra 62.7% (September 2026) to show the rapid rise. Accent colour only for the tier labels, not the dots.
chart_specs.interactions: Hover/tap a dot to show the exact comparison (e.g. 'GPT-4o alone 82.9% vs doctors with GPT-4o 71.4%; exploratory secondary analysis'), date, provenance tag and a link to the footnote. Legend toggles to fade one evidence class. Keyboard focusable dots; mobile shows the comparison in a sheet below the chart.
chart_specs.caveat_label: Positions are qualitative tiers, not a common scale. Several 'ahead' dots compare AI with machines (GenCast vs ECMWF ENS) or average people (Waymo), not the best humans. IMO 2026 grading is company-reported; ICPC 12/12 and Waymo are vendor-reported. Data as of 7 Nov 2026.

chart_specs.purpose: Show at a glance that the four best-known AGI definitions test four different things, so 'has AI reached AGI?' has no single answer; the last column shows the same AI scoring very differently depending on the test.

chart_specs.encoding: Small editorial table, four rows by three columns (Definition / What it tests / Where AI stands), not a plotted chart. The 'What it tests' cell is set in the accent colour as a short label (Economic output; Percentile of skilled adults; Breadth of thinking; Learning efficiency). The 'Where AI stands' cell carries a provenance chip (Vendor-reported for the OpenAI charter row, Verified for the other three). Optional micro-visual in the Hendrycks row: a 10-cell strip of GPT-5's domain scores showing maths at 10 and memory storage at 0. Stacks to cards on phone width.
chart_specs.interactions: Provenance chip links to the matching footnote. On hover or tap of a row, show the full definition quote (charter wording, Levels thresholds, Hendrycks 'well-educated adult' definition, ARC 'learning efficiency of humans'). No animation.

chart_specs.encoding: Grid of small multiples, each with its own y-axis and a coloured provenance tag in the panel header. chart_specs.purpose: Show that 'AI changing weights' covers distinct kinds of work, place the MIT result in its correct cell (another model's weights, direct edit), and make visible that the 'own weights + direct edit' cell is empty.

chart_specs.encoding: 2x2 grid. Columns: whose weights change (the model's own / another model's). Rows: how (gradient training on self-generated data / direct edit without training on the target). Cells: own+gradient = STaR (2022), Self-Rewarding LMs (2024), SEAL (2025), MASS (Oct 2026); other+direct = ROME/MEMIT (2022), Heretic (optimizer), Text-to-LoRA / Drag-and-Drop (generated by a trained network), MIT Weight-Space Programming (Nov 2026, highlighted in the accent colour); other+gradient = ordinary fine-tuning by people, e.g. Cursor Tab online RL run by the company (vendor-reported); own+direct = empty, labelled 'Not yet shown; MIT lists it as future work'. A side strip outside the grid, 'Weights untouched: code-level self-modification', holds Darwin Gödel Machine (2025), Gödel Agent (2025), AlphaEvolve (2025). Each name carries a small status badge (research toy / benchmark gain / in production) and a provenance tag.
chart_specs.interactions: Hover or tap a name for a one-line description, date and source tag with link. On phones the grid stacks into four labelled cards plus the code strip, with the empty cell kept visible.
chart_specs.caveat_label: Our classification; examples, not a complete census. The MIT result is a blog post, not peer-reviewed.

open_issues: Provenance tags fit imperfectly. STYLE.md's 'Verified' means an independent organisation measured it, but several footnotes here are non-peer-reviewed sources: the MIT blog post (the authors' own measurements, independent of OpenAI, with public logs), arXiv preprints (MASS, DGM, 2607.11020, Drag-and-Drop), and individual commentators' posts (Willison, Goedecke, Honnibal). I tagged them 'Verified' and spelled out the status in each footnote. The editor may want a house rule for preprints and commentary.

Krentsel's rerun is mentioned with an inline link and no footnote. The fact-checker marked his cross-generation multiples (e.g. Astra 22x, Opus 5.5 20x) 'unsupported': they come from OfficeChai describing an X chart, and the original was not checked. None of the four provenance tags honestly fits, so I used no numbers and an inline link. Change this if the site requires footnotes for every source.

No data file exists for the s7-weights-matrix chart. It is a qualitative diagram built from r2-selfweights_landscape.md. Where learned weight generators go is a judgement call: I put them under 'another model, direct edit' because they write weights in one forward pass, though the generator itself is trained by gradient descent. The 'other + gradient' cell uses Cursor Tab (vendor-reported) as its example; an editor may prefer to leave that cell as generic 'ordinary fine-tuning'.

The claim that 'no publicly known frontier chatbot updates its weights from live use' rests on a FutureSearch evidence sheet surfaced via search (not fetched directly), an AI-2027 tracker entry, and limited searches (about 15). Lab release notes were not crawled exhaustively.

STaR (2022), ROME (2022) and Self-Rewarding LMs details were not re-fetched in round 2. STaR's source is from prior knowledge, per the topic file. They are named only as examples, without numbers; verify before charting them with dates.
